regimes.name: UAE Personal Data Protection Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021)
regimes.note: In force since 2 January 2022. Sources conflict on whether the Executive Regulations have been issued; the most authoritative 2026 sources say not yet. The UAE Data Office was folded into the federal Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority (14 June 2026). Treat the law as binding.

regimes.name: UAE Corporate Tax (Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022)
regimes.note: Registration and annual return for every taxable business, including free zone companies. Corporate Tax records must be kept for 7 years after the end of the tax period; VAT records for 5 years.

regimes.name: UAE cybercrime law (Federal Decree-Law No. 34 of 2021)
regimes.note: Sets the offences your controls protect against, and the line you must not cross when testing systems.

regimes.name: Hidden connections (IE-REF-023)
regimes.status: Good practice, mapped to ISO/IEC 27001, IEC 62443 and UAE IA
regimes.note: Remote support tools, USB sticks, contractor laptops, extra internet links and shared PCs are common hidden routes into a business. Most are added for convenience and are invisible to office IT monitoring; a site walk is the reliable way to find them.

regimes.name: Real beneficiary rules (Cabinet Resolution No. 109 of 2023; penalties Cabinet Decision No. 132 of 2023)
regimes.note: Every company licensed on the mainland or in a non-financial free zone keeps registers of real beneficiaries, partners or shareholders and nominee managers, and files them with its licensing authority. DIFC and ADGM have their own rules.

regimes.name: UAE e-invoicing (Ministerial Decisions No. 243 and 244 of 2025; penalties Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025)
regimes.note: Covers sales to businesses and government, VAT-registered or not. Consumer-only sales are excluded until a further ministerial decision. Revenue AED 50m+: appoint an Accredited Service Provider by 30 Oct 2026 (extended from 31 Jul), live 1 Jan 2027. Everyone else: provider by 31 Mar 2027, live 1 Jul 2027. Missing the appointment or go-live: AED 5,000 per month.

regimes.name: CBUAE Operational Risk Management Regulation (Circular C 1/2026)
regimes.status: Contractual: the bank passes it to you
regimes.note: Assessment of providers, audit and exit terms, UAE data location, 4-hour and 72-hour incident notice.

regimes.name: UAE Information Assurance Regulation (UAE IA)
regimes.status: Mandatory for government and critical entities; passed to their suppliers by contract
regimes.note: Other entities are strongly recommended to adopt it voluntarily.

regimes.name: Federal Law No. 2 of 2019 on ICT in Health Fields
regimes.note: Applies across the UAE including free zones. Article 13: health data stays in the UAE unless an exception under Ministerial Decision No. 51 of 2021 applies; breach carries a fine of AED 500,000 to 700,000.

regimes.name: Abu Dhabi Healthcare Information and Cyber Security Standard (ADHICS)
regimes.status: Mandatory if you store or process health information from Abu Dhabi
regimes.note: Department of Health scope covers any entity handling Abu Dhabi health information, not only hospitals.

AI.name: Uses AI to predict or decide about people

regimes.name: UAE Charter for the Development and Use of AI (2024)
regimes.note: No standalone UAE AI law as of November 2026. The federal Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority was established on 14 June 2026 and will set AI and data standards.

regimes.name: UAE PDPL as applied to AI
regimes.note: Personal data used to train or run models must have a lawful basis, be minimised and be secured.

regimes.name: GCAA unmanned aircraft regulations
regimes.note: Operator authorisation, approval for flights, security clearance for camera-equipped flights, insurance. GCAA Safety Decision 2026-03 suspended drone authorisations from 28 Feb 2026; Issue 03 (27 Apr 2026) lifted only Part SPO operations. Operators report commercial flying resumed 30 Jun 2026, but no GCAA lifting notice was located: confirm current status with GCAA before relying on any approval.

regimes.name: Federal and emirate autonomous vehicle rules
regimes.note: Federal Decree-Law No. 14 of 2024 on Traffic Regulation provides for self-driving vehicles; on 2 Sep 2026 the Cabinet approved federal rules for their inspection, registration, licensing and testing (some outlets call it a federal law). Emirate rules still apply: Dubai Law No. 9 of 2023 (RTA), Abu Dhabi ITC permits, Ras Al Khaimah Law No. 1 of 2026 (RAKTA).

regimes.name: UN R155 and R156, ISO/SAE 21434
regimes.note: Vehicle cybersecurity and software-update management systems required for type approval in UNECE markets.

regimes.name: ISA/IEC 62443
regimes.status: International standard; often required by critical-infrastructure buyers
regimes.note: Zones and conduits, secure remote access, hardened devices, supplier security levels.

regimes.name: CBUAE Insurance Brokers' Regulation (in force 15 Feb 2025) and Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025
regimes.note: Only CBUAE-licensed brokers may broke onshore UAE risks. Brokers may not collect premiums, claims or refunds; need CBUAE no-objection to outsource material activities and may not outsource outside the UAE; must appoint a CBUAE-approved external auditor; must protect personal data and maintain cyber security.

regimes.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (PCI Security Standards Council)
regimes.status: Contractual: required by your card provider (acquirer) under the card scheme rules
regimes.note: v4.0.1 is the only active version (v4.0 retired 31 Dec 2024) and every former future-dated requirement has applied since 31 Mar 2025. The Council consulted on the next version from 3 Jun to 20 Jul 2026; no release date is set. Small merchants usually confirm compliance once a year with a Self-Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ). The right SAQ depends on how you take cards: standalone terminal (B or B-IP), payment link or hosted checkout (A), virtual terminal on a separate computer (C-VT), payment software connected to the internet (C), or card data kept in your own systems (D). The security code (CVV) must never be kept after a payment is approved.

regimes.name: Your card provider's requirements (UAE)
regimes.status: Contractual: set by your merchant agreement
regimes.note: Your acquirer decides which SAQ applies, how you submit it and the deadline; ask them in writing. Magnati, a UAE acquirer, states that PCI DSS is mandated in the UAE by the CBUAE; IE has not located the CBUAE instrument itself, so treat this as acquirer-stated. Merchant agreements commonly make the merchant responsible for its own PCI DSS compliance and costs, even when card processing is outsourced.

XB.name: Holds data on people outside the UAE

regimes.name: EU GDPR and UK GDPR (where you offer services to people there)
regimes.note: Can apply to a UAE business that targets EU or UK residents.

DD.name: Due diligence compliance check (sale, partner or funding)

regimes.name: Due diligence by a buyer, investor or lender
regimes.status: Not a law: the compliance checks the other side will run
regimes.note: These questions check the legal records and controls a due diligence team asks for. Scored separately from the compliance result. IE does not value businesses, advise on deal terms or act in the transaction.

regimes.name: UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021)
regimes.note: Written employment contracts and end-of-service gratuity are legal duties; due diligence checks both.

regimes.name: Buyer supplier questionnaires
regimes.note: Larger buyers send security and compliance questionnaires before award; a ready supplier pack shortens the cycle.

EXPAND.name: Expanding to a new site, emirate or country

regimes.name: Licensing in each new jurisdiction
regimes.note: Free zone licences generally limit where you may trade; mainland or another country needs its own licence and permits.

PRM.name: Premises systems (CCTV, door entry, alarms, lifts, tills, signage)

regimes.name: ISA/IEC 62443 principles for building systems
regimes.status: International standard; good practice for premises systems
regimes.note: SIM cards and 4G routers in lift, fire and building panels, and cameras viewable from phones, bypass office networks and monitoring. Keep an inventory, a named owner and a change rule for every connection.

screener.q: Are you thinking of selling, bringing in a partner or handing the business over in the next two years?
screener.lead: Why we ask: a buyer or new partner will run due diligence on your licences, records, contracts and data. We check those compliance points so nothing is missed.

screener.q: Do you plan to raise investment or take a business loan in the next 12 months?
screener.lead: Why we ask: investors and lenders check the same compliance points as a buyer.

screener.q: Do you want to win larger contracts (government, big companies) in the next 12 months?
screener.lead: Why we ask: larger buyers send a security and compliance questionnaire before they award work.

screener.q: Are you planning a new branch, another emirate or another country?
screener.lead: Why we ask: each new location can bring its own licence, permits and data rules.

screener.q: Who do you sell to, or want to sell to?
Do you collect or handle health, medical or wellbeing information about people?
Do you use AI to predict, score or decide things about people?
Do you operate drones or other unmanned aircraft?
Do you operate driverless or remotely operated vehicles?
Does your premises have CCTV, door entry, alarms, building controls, lift or fire panels, card tills or digital signage?
Do you run or supply connected physical systems (building controls, industrial equipment, charging or fleet control systems)?
Do you arrange, sell or introduce insurance?
Do you hold personal data on people living outside the UAE (for example EU or UK customers)?

text: Every Critical control Met (answered Yes and management will sign for it)
No High control missing (No, Not sure, or Yes that management will not confirm)

fact_rule.text: Every regulation and current-development entry is re-checked against a primary or two independent sources at least every 90 days. A report that relies on an entry older than 90 days is not issued.

retention.answers_file: Deleted once the report is issued
retention.text: Your answers and IE's copy of this report are held only in the UAE. IE deletes the answers once the report is issued and its copy of the report 90 days after issue. You keep your own copy.

disclaimer: This report is advice based only on the information you gave us. We did not inspect your systems, documents or evidence, and we are not responsible for risks we were not told about or for answers that were inaccurate.
We do not make changes to your systems. Your appointed staff member carries out every step; we guide them through it in a walkthrough session.
We never ask for, accept or record passwords, MFA codes, recovery codes or encryption keys. If one is ever shown or sent to us by mistake, change it straight away.
Regulation screening shows which rules are likely to apply. It is not legal advice, a valuation or a certification. Confirm licensing questions with the relevant authority or your lawyer.
These terms are set out in full in section 2A of our Terms of Business (IE-TOB-002).

questions.title: Valid trade licence covering services
questions.question: Is your trade licence valid, and does it cover every service you sell?
questions.why: Buyers, regulators and insurers check the licence first; trading outside it voids contracts and cover.
fix: Check the licence expiry date and the listed activities against your service list.
If an activity is missing, apply to your free zone or DED to add it before quoting.
Put the renewal date on a renewal register with reminders at 60, 30 and 7 days.
Keep a current copy ready to send with any tender response.
questions.ie_service: Business Security Audit: renewal register set-up
questions.evidence: Current licence or registry extract; activity titles matched to the service list

questions.title: Filings, tax and renewals up to date
questions.question: Are all statutory filings, tax registrations and renewals up to date, with nothing overdue?
questions.why: Late filings bring fines and strike-off notices, and buyers check public registers.
fix: List every legal date: licence, visas, establishment card, audit, Corporate Tax, VAT.
Clear anything overdue first, including penalties.
Give one accountant responsibility for statutory filings.
Review the list every month.
questions.ie_service: Business Security Audit: renewal register set-up
questions.evidence: Registry filing history with no overdue items; Calendar entries with owner and reminder for each date; Corporate tax and VAT registration certificates; Filing and payment receipts for the last period

questions.title: Named security owner
questions.question: Is one named person accountable for information security, with the time and authority to act?
questions.why: Regulated buyers want a named security contact who can answer for controls and incidents.
fix: Name the person in writing, with a deputy.
Record their responsibilities in the security policy.
Give the bank their name and contact details at onboarding.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: named security owner

questions.title: Approved information security policy
questions.question: Do you have a written information security policy, approved by management and reviewed at least once a year?
questions.why: Banks, government entities and health regulators all ask suppliers for their policy first.
fix: Adopt a short policy set: acceptable use, access and MFA, devices, data handling, incidents, backup, suppliers.
Have management approve and date it.
Brief every person who works on client accounts.
Diary the annual review.
questions.evidence: Approved, dated policy set

questions.title: PI and cyber insurance
questions.question: Do you hold professional indemnity insurance, and have you decided on cyber insurance, at levels your clients would accept?
questions.why: Regulated buyers require proof of cover before contract and check a supplier's financial standing.
fix: Ask the bank or tender for its minimum limits.
Get two quotes from a broker for PI and cyber cover.
Bind cover before the contract starts and keep the certificate ready to send.
Put the renewal date on the renewal register.
questions.evidence: PI certificate with limit, territory and activities; Policy or a recorded decision not to buy

questions.title: Financial statements available
questions.question: Could you show a client your latest financial statements if asked?
questions.why: Banks and government entities check that suppliers they rely on are financially sound.
fix: Prepare the latest annual accounts, audited if your licence requires it.
Agree with your accountant what can be shared and under NDA.
Keep a one-page financial summary ready for tenders.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: financial statements available

questions.title: Bank and CBUAE audit rights in contract
questions.question: Would your standard contract accept a client's audit and inspection rights, including by its regulator?
questions.why: Banks (CBUAE), insurers and government entities write audit access into supplier contracts.
fix: Read your terms for audit, inspection and regulator access clauses.
Add a clause allowing the client, its auditors and its regulator to audit on reasonable notice.
Have the terms legally reviewed.
questions.ie_service: Contract review (GRC advisory with legal partner)
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: bank and CBUAE audit rights in contract

questions.title: Obligations flowed to subcontractors
questions.question: If you use subcontractors or partners, do your contracts with them pass on the same security, confidentiality and audit obligations?
questions.why: Regulators require the same protections to flow down to subcontractors.
fix: List every subcontractor that could touch bank data or systems.
Add flow-down clauses: confidentiality, security, audit, incident notice, no further subcontracting without approval.
Get each subcontractor to sign.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: obligations flowed to subcontractors

questions.title: Data processing agreement
questions.question: Do you have a data processing agreement ready for clients whose personal data you handle?
questions.why: UAE PDPL requires processors to act on documented instructions; regulated clients will not share personal data without one.
fix: Adopt a data processing agreement template under the UAE PDPL (and DIFC or ADGM law where relevant).
Reference it in your terms of business.
Keep a record of which clients have signed it.
questions.evidence: DPA template and a reference to it in the terms

questions.title: Exit plan: return or delete data
questions.question: Do you have an exit plan: at contract end, return or securely delete the client's data and hand over the service?
questions.why: Banks, insurers and government entities must be able to leave a supplier without losing data or service.
fix: Write a one-page exit plan: what is returned, what is deleted, in what time, and how deletion is confirmed.
Add the exit commitment to your contract.
Test it once with a dummy client folder.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: exit plan: return or delete data

questions.title: Data location known, UAE possible
questions.question: Do you know where client data you hold is stored, and could you keep it in the UAE if required?
questions.why: Banks, government entities and health law (Federal Law No. 2 of 2019) can require UAE storage.
fix: List every system that would hold bank data and its storage region.
Choose UAE-region services (for example Microsoft UAE North) or keep no copy outside the bank's environment.
State the data location in your proposal.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: data location known, UAE possible

questions.title: Confidentiality agreements signed
questions.question: Has everyone who could access client information signed a confidentiality agreement?
questions.why: Regulated clients require confidentiality from everyone with access, including contractors.
fix: Add a confidentiality clause to employment and contractor agreements.
Get existing staff and contractors to sign.
Keep signed copies on file.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: confidentiality agreements signed

questions.title: Background screening
questions.question: Are staff and contractors background-checked at hiring, and can they complete a client's screening if asked?
questions.why: Banks, government entities and health providers screen people who access their systems.
fix: Define basic checks at hiring: identity, right to work, references.
Agree that staff will complete a client's screening (for example a police clearance certificate) when requested.
Record that the checks were done, not the results.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: background screening

questions.title: Annual security awareness training
questions.question: Does everyone who uses company systems get basic security training at least once a year?
questions.why: Most attacks on small businesses start with a message that tricks a person.
fix: Run a short annual course: phishing, passwords and MFA, reporting incidents.
Record names and completion dates.
Repeat for new joiners within their first month.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: annual security awareness training

questions.title: Same-day leaver access removal
questions.question: When someone leaves, is all their access removed on their last day?
questions.why: Former staff with live access are a common cause of loss and fraud.
fix: Keep a list of every account each person has.
Use a leaver checklist; disable accounts on the last day.
Review all accounts every quarter.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: same-day leaver access removal

questions.title: MFA on all accounts
questions.question: Is multi-factor authentication on for every account that reaches company or customer data: email, cloud, banking, admin?
questions.why: Account takeover is the commonest way into a small business.
fix: List every business account.
Turn on MFA with an authenticator app or key; avoid SMS where possible.
Enforce it centrally (Google Admin or Microsoft Entra Conditional Access).
Record the method per account.
questions.evidence: Account list with MFA method per account

questions.title: Password manager, no shared accounts
questions.question: Are passwords unique and held in a password manager, with no shared accounts?
questions.why: Shared and reused passwords defeat every other access control.
fix: Deploy a business password manager with MFA on it.
Replace shared logins with named accounts.
Move credentials in and change each to a generated password.
questions.evidence: Password manager in use; no credentials in email

questions.title: Encrypted laptops and phones
questions.question: Are all laptops and phones encrypted, with recovery keys held safely?
questions.why: A lost unencrypted laptop or phone exposes every customer and company record on it.
fix: Turn on BitLocker or Device Encryption on Windows, FileVault on Mac, a passcode on phones.
Store recovery keys in the password manager or the company admin console, never only on the device.
Confirm with manage-bde -status C: and keep the result.
questions.evidence: Encryption, update and anti-malware status screenshots

questions.title: Work devices not shared
questions.question: Are work devices used only by authorised staff, and never shared with family or others?
questions.why: Customers and buyers ask whether devices are used only by authorised staff.
fix: Issue work devices to named people only.
Give family members their own device or a separate account.
State the rule in the acceptable use policy.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: work devices not shared

questions.title: Supported and patched systems
questions.question: Are operating systems and software supported and patched within 14 days (critical fixes faster)?
questions.why: Unpatched and unsupported systems are the easiest way in for attackers.
fix: Turn on automatic updates on every device.
Replace any unsupported operating system or software.
Check update status monthly.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: supported and patched systems

questions.title: Endpoint protection on every device
questions.question: Is anti-malware or endpoint protection running and up to date on every device?
questions.why: Malware on one device can reach every account and file the business uses.
fix: Use Microsoft Defender or an equivalent endpoint product on every device.
Manage it centrally so alerts are seen.
Check weekly that every device reports in.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: endpoint protection on every device

questions.title: SPF, DKIM and enforced DMARC
questions.question: If you use your own email domain, does it publish SPF, DKIM and an enforced DMARC policy?
questions.why: Without them anyone can send email as you, including fake invoices to your customers.
fix: Enable DKIM signing in your email platform.
Publish DMARC at p=none with reports, then move to quarantine, then reject.
Protect parked domains with a null SPF record and DMARC reject.
questions.evidence: Public DNS records for every domain, sending or not

questions.title: Independent, tested backups
questions.question: Are backups kept independently and encrypted, with a restore tested at least every quarter?
questions.why: Ransomware and lost devices are survivable only with a backup you know works.
fix: Keep a second copy separate from the working device or tenant, encrypted.
Restore one real file each quarter and log the result.
Fix and re-test any failure.
questions.evidence: Restore test record in the last quarter

questions.title: Asset inventory
questions.question: Do you keep an up-to-date list of devices, systems and cloud services in use?
questions.why: You cannot protect, or answer a client about, systems you have not listed.
fix: List devices, software and cloud services with owner and end-of-support date.
Update it when anything is added or removed.
Review it quarterly.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: asset inventory

questions.title: Limited admin rights, separate accounts
questions.question: Are administrator rights limited to the people who need them, using separate admin accounts?
questions.why: Everyday accounts with admin rights turn one phishing email into full control.
fix: Remove admin rights from everyday accounts.
Create separate admin accounts with MFA for the few who need them.
Review admin membership quarterly.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: limited admin rights, separate accounts

questions.title: Security alerts logged and reviewed
questions.question: Are sign-in and security alerts logged and reviewed?
questions.why: Detection depends on someone looking at the alerts.
fix: Turn on audit logging in your email and cloud platform.
Set alerts for risky sign-ins and mailbox forwarding rules.
Review alerts weekly, or use a monitored service.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: security alerts logged and reviewed

questions.title: Independent vulnerability test
questions.question: Have you had an independent vulnerability scan or penetration test in the last 12 months?
questions.why: Regulated buyers expect tested defences and ask for the summary.
fix: Commission an external vulnerability scan of your internet-facing services.
Fix high and critical findings and re-test.
Keep the summary ready for the bank.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: independent vulnerability test

questions.title: Rules for AI tools
questions.question: Do you have rules for AI tools, so no client or customer data goes into public AI services?
questions.why: Data pasted into a public AI tool leaves your control and your client's.
fix: Write a one-paragraph AI use rule into the acceptable use policy.
List approved business AI tools whose terms exclude training on your data.
Brief staff.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: rules for AI tools

questions.title: Incident response plan
questions.question: Do you have a written plan for what to do if you are hacked, defrauded or lose data, with named roles and contacts?
questions.why: In an incident, minutes matter; a one-page plan stops panic decisions.
fix: Write a short plan: report, contain, assess, notify, recover, review.
Name who does what, with phone numbers.
Run a 30-minute tabletop exercise once a year.
questions.evidence: Incident log, even if empty, with review dates

questions.title: Incident notice fast enough for CBUAE deadlines
questions.question: Could you notify the bank of an incident affecting it fast enough for the bank to meet CBUAE's 4-hour, 24-hour and 72-hour reporting deadlines?
questions.why: Banks must notify CBUAE within 4 hours of events affecting Critical Operations and within 72 hours of high-risk incidents; they pass this down to suppliers.
fix: Commit in your contract to notify the bank within the time it sets (often 1 to 4 hours of awareness).
Keep a notification template: what happened, which services, actions taken, expected recovery.
Make sure partners notify you fast enough to meet it.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: incident notice fast enough for CBUAE deadlines

questions.title: Incident log
questions.question: Do you keep a log of security incidents and near misses, reviewed for lessons?
questions.why: No log means no evidence of control.
fix: Start an incident log, even if it is empty: date, what, impact, action, lesson.
Review it monthly.
Feed lessons into policies and training.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: incident log

questions.title: Tested business continuity plan
questions.question: Do you have a business continuity plan covering loss of systems, premises and key people, tested at least once a year?
questions.why: Regulated buyers depend on your service continuing, including when key staff are unavailable.
fix: Write a short continuity plan: what stops, how you keep serving clients, recovery times.
Name a deputy and set up break-glass access to key accounts.
Test once a year and record the result.
questions.evidence: Business continuity statement and sealed access arrangement

questions.title: Own suppliers assessed
questions.question: Do you assess the security of your own critical suppliers (cloud, software, subcontractors)?
questions.why: Your client's supply chain includes your suppliers.
fix: List your critical suppliers.
Check each one's security terms or certifications.
Review yearly and keep a record.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: own suppliers assessed

questions.title: Privacy notice and PDPL compliance
questions.question: Have you published an accurate privacy notice and do you meet your obligations under the UAE PDPL?
questions.why: Customers and partners expect it, and the PDPL applies to every business handling personal data.
fix: Publish a privacy notice that matches what you actually do.
Keep a one-page record of what personal data you hold, why, where and for how long.
Name who handles data subject requests.
questions.evidence: Live privacy notice with no placeholders

questions.title: Certification or dated plan
questions.question: Do you hold a security certification (for example ISO/IEC 27001), or have a dated plan to get one?
questions.why: Certification shortens a buyer's due diligence; a plan shows direction.
fix: Decide which certification your buyers ask for.
Run a gap assessment and set a target date.
Share the plan with the bank if not yet certified.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: certification or dated plan

questions.title: Independent review in last 12 months
questions.question: Has your security been independently reviewed in the last 12 months?
questions.why: An independent review is a buyer's assurance that your answers are true.
fix: Commission an independent review against a recognised standard.
Fix the findings and keep the summary.
Repeat every year.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: independent review in last 12 months

questions.title: E-invoicing ready for your phase date
questions.question: Do you know your UAE e-invoicing phase date, and have you chosen or appointed an Accredited Service Provider?
questions.why: E-invoicing for sales to businesses and government becomes mandatory in phases from 1 January 2027; missing the provider appointment costs AED 5,000 a month (Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025).

refs.B2B: Ministerial Decisions No. 243 and 244 of 2025; Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025

fix: Check your phase: revenue over AED 50m goes live 1 Jan 2027 (provider by 30 Oct 2026); everyone else 1 Jul 2027 (provider by 31 Mar 2027).
Ask your accounting software supplier whether it connects to an Accredited Service Provider.
Put both dates on the renewal register.
questions.ie_service: Business Security Audit: renewal register set-up
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: e-invoicing ready for your phase date

questions.title: Business accounts owned by the business
questions.question: Are your business accounts (WhatsApp Business, delivery platforms, social media, bank app, domain) registered to the business, protected with 2-step verification, and not tied to one person's personal phone or email?
questions.why: If the one person who owns the number leaves or loses the phone, the business loses its customers and its money channel.
fix: List every business account and whose phone or email it is linked to.
Move each one to a business phone number or business email, and add a second admin where the platform allows.
Turn on 2-step verification and store recovery codes in the password manager.
questions.evidence: Registrar account in company name with MFA

questions.title: Sector permits current
questions.question: Do you hold every sector permit your work needs (for example food safety, workshop, health, transport or aviation permits), and are they in date?
questions.why: A missing sector permit can close the business regardless of its trade licence.
fix: List the permits your activity needs from the relevant authority (for example ADAFSA or the municipality for food, the municipality for workshops).
Check each expiry date.
Add them to the renewal register with reminders.
questions.ie_service: Business Security Audit: renewal register set-up
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: sector permits current

questions.title: Payment change requests verified
questions.question: Before paying a new or changed bank account, do you confirm it by phone using a number you already hold?
questions.why: Fake 'our bank details have changed' messages are the commonest fraud against small businesses.
fix: Make it a rule: no payment to new or changed bank details without a call-back on a known number.
Tell suppliers and staff about the rule.
Use your bank's payee confirmation feature where offered.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: payment change requests verified

questions.title: Government information classified and handled by label
questions.question: Do you label government information by classification and handle each level by set rules (storage, sharing, disposal)?
questions.why: Government entities classify information and expect suppliers to protect it to the same level.
fix: Adopt the entity's classification levels in your data handling policy.
Label documents and folders by level.
Restrict confidential material to named staff and approved systems.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: government information classified and handled by label

questions.title: Government data kept in UAE
questions.question: Is government data you handle stored and processed only in the UAE, on services approved by the entity?
questions.why: Government entities typically require UAE data residency and approved cloud services.

refs.GOV: UAE IA Regulation (cloud and third-party controls)

fix: List the systems that would hold government data and their regions.
Use UAE-region services or the entity's own systems.
Record the data location in your proposal.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: government data kept in UAE

questions.title: Incident notice to the government entity

questions.title: Buyer requirements checked
questions.question: Have you checked what security standard your target buyers require (for example ISO/IEC 27001 or UAE IA) and set a dated plan to meet it?
questions.why: Some contracts are closed to suppliers without a named standard.
fix: List your target buyers and what they ask suppliers for.
Compare with what you have.
Set a dated plan for the gap.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: buyer requirements checked

questions.title: Licence and permits checked for the new location
questions.question: Before trading in the new location, have you confirmed the licence, permits and data rules that apply there?
questions.why: Trading outside your licence area risks fines and voided contracts.
fix: Ask the authority in the new location what licence and permits you need.
Check whether customer data may move there.
Add the new dates to the renewal register.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: licence and permits checked for the new location

questions.title: Controls extend to the new site
questions.question: Will the new site use the same accounts, MFA, encrypted devices and backups as the existing business?
questions.why: New sites set up in a hurry are where controls slip.
fix: Write a short setup checklist for new sites.
Use it before the site opens.
Re-run this review six months after opening.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: controls extend to the new site

questions.title: Remote support tools controlled
questions.question: Do you know every remote support tool (for example TeamViewer or AnyDesk) installed on your computers, CCTV recorder, till or building PCs, and does each one need someone on site to approve a connection?
questions.why: Unattended remote access set up by an installer or vendor lets anyone with the login connect without you knowing; it is the commonest forgotten way in.
fix: List every device with a remote support tool and who uses it.
Remove the ones nobody needs; set the rest to need on-site approval and MFA.
Ask IE for a Hidden Connections Walk to find tools nobody remembers.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: remote support tools controlled

walk.look_for: Remote support tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk) on the CCTV, BMS or POS PC
walk.ask: Who can connect to this PC without someone here clicking accept?

questions.title: USB sticks controlled
questions.question: Are USB sticks and other removable drives limited to approved ones, scanned before use, and never used to move files between the CCTV recorder, tills or office PCs?
questions.why: USB sticks carry malware between systems that are otherwise kept apart.
fix: Decide which tasks really need a USB stick and issue approved ones only.
Turn on automatic scanning or device control on PCs.
Use a secure transfer method instead where possible.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: uSB sticks controlled

walk.look_for: USB sticks by the CCTV recorder, tills or engineering PC
walk.ask: Where did this stick last go, and what runs from it?

questions.title: Outside companies' connections listed
questions.question: Do you keep a list of outside companies and contractors that connect to your systems or Wi-Fi (including their laptops and VPNs), and review it at least every six months?
questions.why: Contractor laptops and VPN tunnels on your network are connections you do not control.
fix: List each company that connects, how and when.
Put visitors and contractors on a separate guest Wi-Fi.
Remove access for anyone no longer working for you.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: outside companies' connections listed

walk.look_for: Contractor laptops on the office Wi-Fi
walk.ask: Which outside companies connect, how, and when was that list last checked?

questions.title: Every internet connection known
questions.question: Do you know every internet connection your business uses (including backup 5G routers, satellite such as Starlink, and mobile hotspots), who installed each one and who manages it?
questions.why: A second internet link bypasses your firewall and any monitoring, so nobody sees what crosses it.
fix: Count every internet connection, including backups and hotspots.
Remove ones nobody needs; put the rest behind the same firewall rules.
Name an owner who must approve any new connection.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: every internet connection known

walk.look_for: A second internet link: satellite dish (Starlink is licensed in the UAE since 28 Aug 2026), 5G router, hotspot
walk.ask: How many internet connections do you have, and who installed each one?

questions.title: Shared PCs kept to one job
questions.question: Is any one computer used for several jobs at once (for example email, banking, till or system admin and viewing CCTV), and if so are those uses separated with their own accounts?
questions.why: One phishing email on a shared PC reaches banking, tills and cameras at the same time.
fix: List what each shared PC is used for.
Move banking and admin to a separate device or at least a separate account.
Turn on web filtering on PCs that run tills, CCTV or building systems.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: shared PCs kept to one job

walk.look_for: One shared PC used for email, banking, POS admin and CCTV
walk.ask: What else is this PC used for?

questions.title: No unknown SIM cards in panels
questions.question: Do you know of every SIM card or 4G router inside your lift, fire alarm, building control, generator or charger panels, who pays for it and who can connect through it?
questions.why: A SIM in a panel is an internet link that office IT does not see and usually no one owns.
fix: Ask your landlord, facilities manager and each panel supplier which panels have a SIM.
Record each one with its owner and purpose.
Ask IE for a Hidden Connections Walk to check the panels in person.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: no unknown SIM cards in panels

walk.look_for: 4G router, SIM card or antenna in a lift, fire alarm, BMS or generator panel
walk.ask: Is there a SIM anywhere in the building that IT does not pay for?

questions.title: Cameras and building screens not open to the internet
questions.question: If you can view cameras or building systems from a phone, is that through the supplier's secure app with a strong password and 2-step verification (not an open port), and are recorder or control screens never used to browse the web?
questions.why: Cameras and recorders reachable from the internet are scanned for constantly, and a browsing session on a control screen brings malware straight to it.
fix: Check how phone viewing is set up; close any port forwarding on your router.
Change default passwords and turn on 2-step verification in the camera app.
Block web browsing on recorder and control screens.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: cameras and building screens not open to the internet

walk.look_for: CCTV, BMS or signage screens used to browse, or viewable from a phone
walk.ask: Can you see your cameras from your phone? Show me how.

questions.title: Beneficial owner register filed
questions.question: Does the business keep its registers of real beneficiaries and shareholders, filed with your licensing authority and updated within the deadline after any change?
questions.why: It is a legal duty for mainland and free zone companies, with fines under Cabinet Decision No. 132 of 2023, and banks check it when opening accounts.
fix: Ask your licensing authority or registered agent for your current filing.
Check every owner and manager listed is correct.
Put the update rule on the renewal register: any change must be filed promptly.
questions.ie_service: Business Security Audit: renewal register set-up
questions.evidence: UBO or PSC filing confirmation

questions.title: Record of personal data kept
questions.question: Do you keep a simple record of the personal data you hold (customers, staff, suppliers): what it is, why you hold it, where it is stored and who can see it?
questions.why: The UAE PDPL (Article 7) requires a record of personal data that the regulator can ask to see, and you cannot protect data you have not listed.
fix: List each type of personal data and where it is kept.
Note why you hold it and how long you keep it.
Review the list once a year.
questions.evidence: One-page data map: what, where, why, how long

questions.title: Data breach reporting ready
questions.question: If personal data were lost or stolen, do you know that you must report it to the UAE Data Office and, where it harms them, tell the people affected, and who in the business would do it?
questions.why: The UAE PDPL (Article 9) makes reporting a personal data breach mandatory; delay makes the harm and the penalty worse.
fix: Name who decides whether a breach is reportable.
Add the reporting step and contact to your incident plan.
Keep a short notification template ready.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: data breach reporting ready

questions.title: Large payments need two people
questions.question: Do payments above a set amount, and any urgent or unusual payment request, need approval by a second person before they are sent?
questions.why: Fraudsters impersonate owners, suppliers and even banks to rush one person into paying; a second approver is the cheapest stop.
fix: Set an amount above which two people must approve.
Treat any 'urgent, keep it quiet' request as suspicious and verify by phone.
Use your bank's dual-approval feature where offered.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: large payments need two people

questions.title: Website kept updated and protected
questions.question: If you have a website, are the platform and plugins updated at least monthly, and is every admin login protected by 2-step verification?
questions.why: Out-of-date website software is attacked automatically within days of a flaw being published, and a hacked site damages your name with customers and search engines.
fix: Ask whoever built the site who keeps it updated, and agree a monthly update.
Turn on 2-step verification for every admin login and remove old accounts.
Keep a recent backup of the site.
questions.evidence: Record, screenshot or document that shows: website kept updated and protected
